item.title: Le busca cinco patas al gato para justificar lo injustificable.
item.dc:creator: xynova
item.description: A fifth leg appears only when absurd excuses try to prop up the indefensible.
item.sync:pageSocial:
"Le busca cinco patas al gato para justificar lo injustificable."
❓ You are inventing non-existent variables to force a broken logic fit, rather than admitting a simple mistake. It is like trying to give a cat a fifth leg to justify its wobbly walk. You use it when a politician offers convoluted arguments for a controversial policy, or when a child gives a far-fetched excuse for not doing their homework.
AND: If it requires five miracles to make sense, it is just wrong. You hear it when a colleague explains a missed deadline through a chain of cosmic coincidences. Or when a vendor spins a yarn about why the server crashed, making it sound like an act of God rather than a simple oversight.
🔤 IN ENGLISH: • Grasping at straws • Making flimsy excuses • Trying to explain away • Putting lipstick on a pig

item.title: Miente hasta cuando dice la verdad.
item.dc:creator: xynova
item.description: A sly speaker faces a deeply skeptical listener; their history always speaks louder than their words.
item.sync:pageSocial:
"Miente hasta cuando dice la verdad."
❓ Your reputation filter is on: past lies distort present facts, so you filter everything through a speaker's history, not objective merit. You use it when a politician states an obvious truth but still gets doubted, or when a colleague with a history of dishonesty makes a factual claim and you still don't believe them.
AND: Trust takes a lifetime to build and a single second to break. Someone always late finally has a genuine family emergency, but people still roll their eyes. Or a friend who always inflates their achievements tells a simple, true story about meeting a celebrity, and everyone just nods politely, then changes the subject.
🔤 IN ENGLISH: • You cannot trust them as far as you can throw them. • Take everything they say with a grain of salt. • They are a pathological liar.

item.title: La verdad es hija de Dios.
item.dc:creator: xynova
item.description: Truth is not a story you control; it is a sovereign force that eventually reveals itself, like a veiled figure stepping into light.
item.sync:pageSocial:
"La verdad es hija de Dios."
❓ Truth is an independent force. You cannot edit or spin it to fit your timeline. It exists as an objective, self-revealing reality, not something you manage. You use it when people argue over facts, confident the real truth will eventually emerge. You also use it to reassure someone wronged by lies that their truth will find its way out.
AND: Some facts simply refuse to stay buried. A colleague might quietly patch a system bug without telling anyone, but the error logs always speak for themselves. A family member might try to hide a minor dent, only for it to catch the light during a routine wash.
🔤 IN ENGLISH: • Truth will out. • The truth always comes out in the wash. • What's done in the dark will be brought to light.

item.title: Stable Enough to Remain Unpredictable
item.dc:creator: xynova
item.description: As long as the screaming stays within the institutional comfort band, it is considered a leadership style. The cabinet has officially reclassified his outbursts as acceptable variance.
item.sync:pageSocial:
"Stable Enough to Remain Unpredictable"
❓ The committee mistakes a weather pattern for a personality. They prioritize continuity over psychological fitness, so rage always gets rebranded as a tolerable leadership trait.
AND: The meeting was all about the decibels. Nobody raised impulse control or reality-contact; too messy for a standard assessment. Assessors checked whether the screaming fit the historical average. Inside the approved range, the green stamp lands: STABLE. The institution does not need a healthy leader. It needs the chaos to stay inside the budget.
🟣 W25: Reptilocracy 🦎🏛️
This is part of an experiment: we are keeping count of how many scenes it takes before we agree that leaders with real power should prove they are psychologically fit to hold it.
By turning our instincts and hive habits into animals, the project asks why we still let untested nervous systems run entire societies.

item.title: 🔄 How bystanders learn to sustain a blamer
item.dc:creator: xynova
item.description: When a person cannot register their own reflection, “I caused this” is never an option. Fault lands on everyone else, and silent witnesses become the blank mirrors that sustain the cycle.
item.sync:pageSocial:
The Mirror That Only Blames
A vampire checks the mirror after a feeding. The glass stays empty, so the mess must be the furniture, the light, or the people standing there.
That is the tell in real life. "I caused this" never makes the menu. Every crisis gets a culprit scan of colleagues, partners, or kids, and the nearest face wins.
✜ Bystanders learn fast. Point at the damage and you become the next target. People freeze, swallow objections, and quietly clean up so the blind person never has to see it.
✜ Silence is not neutral. Each quiet witness becomes another blank mirror, proof from the inside that nothing is wrong. The witness pays in held breath and polished flat exhaustion.
The loop is paid by everyone except the person who cannot reflect. Accountability needs someone who refuses to be a blank surface. You cannot fix a missing reflection by hiding the damage.
Who in your life keeps handing you the bill?
#BlameDeflection #AccountabilityGap #RealityCheck #SeeTheGame

item.title: Caimán no come caimán.
item.dc:creator: xynova
item.description: You don’t build a name by burning the competitor’s house. An older peer pulls you aside in the hallway with a quiet warning after a tense meeting.
item.sync:pageSocial:
"Caimán no come caimán."
❓ You operate in a tough world, but you don't attack your own kind. This is mutual non-aggression among peers, a code of professional courtesy. You do not throw a colleague under the bus to score a quick point. You use it when you warn a rival to back off because you share common turf, or when a startup founder chooses not to publicly trash a competitor's product.
AND: Rival agency founders share a drink at a trade show and still keep the unspoken rules. Same instinct when a peer could sink your pitch in front of a client and chooses silence instead.
🔤 IN ENGLISH: • There's honor among thieves • We protect our own • You don't mess with your own kind • Never throw your own under the bus

item.title: The Bridge Is Open
item.dc:creator: xynova
item.description: The leader did not lie; reality simply failed to align with his remarks. We do not question his sanity; we only wonder why the landscape is being so difficult.
item.sync:pageSocial:
"The Bridge Is Open"
❓ The bridge is open, provided you ignore the chasm. Institutions watch a leader's mood harder than they audit psychological fitness. Easier to blame the landscape for non-alignment than to question the man at the podium.
AND: From the podium the bridge is always intact. If the stone fails the speech, that is the terrain's fault, not his. Ants can learn to fly or fall; the official record still shows a successful opening. We debate good days and bad days, smile and shout, and never ask if he can see the gap. The institution does not need a bridge. It needs remarks on the record. The chasm is a technical inconvenience.
